description:
Found by the dual CI (defk-wfi.2), 2026-10-14.

Problem: priv/defk_runtime.h includes <sanitizer/allocator_interface.h> under DEFK_SANITIZE_ADDRESS (for defk_poison_slack: __sanitizer_get_ownership, __sanitizer_get_allocated_size). gcc 14 (Debian trixie, gcc 14.2.0) ships <sanitizer/asan_interface.h> but not allocator_interface.h, so DEFK_SANITIZE=address cannot build with CC=gcc. clang (with libclang-rt-dev) has both.

Seen as: test/sanitize_test.exs 'a normal build compiles none of the sanitizer code in the runtime header' fails with CC=gcc (cc -E -DDEFK_SANITIZE_ADDRESS=1 exits 1), natively on Linux aarch64 and on x86-64. The :sanitize-tagged tests are excluded by default, so only this test shows it.

Options: declare the two functions in the header when the include is missing (__has_include; libasan exports them on gcc too), or document the sanitizer mode as clang-only and make the test and DEFK_SANITIZE say so with a clear error.

Done when: CC=gcc either builds the address-sanitizer mode or rejects it with a clear message, and the test passes with gcc (linux-x86_64-gcc in CI).
title: [BUG] Sanitizer build mode does not compile with gcc: no <sanitizer/allocator_interface.h>
